'''Finite element exterior calculus (FEEC)''' is a [[mathematics|mathematical]] framework that formulates [[finite element method]]s using [[Chain complex|chain complexes]]. Its main application has been a comprehensive theory for finite element methods in [[computational electromagnetism]], computational solid and [[fluid mechanics]]. FEEC was developed in the early 2000s by [[Douglas N. Arnold]], [[Richard S. Falk]] and [[Ragnar Winther]], 
<ref>Arnold, Douglas N., Richard S. Falk, and Ragnar Winther. "[https://conservancy.umn.edu/bitstream/handle/11299/4216/2094.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y Finite element exterior calculus, homological techniques, and applications]." Acta numerica 15 (2006): 1-155.</ref>
<ref>Arnold, Douglas, Richard Falk, and Ragnar Winther. "[https://www.ams.org/bull/2010-47-02/S0273-0979-10-01278-4/S0273-0979-10-01278-4.pdf Finite element exterior calculus: from Hodge theory to numerical stability]." Bulletin of the American mathematical society 47.2 (2010): 281-354.</ref>
<ref>{{cite book |last=Arnold |first=Douglas N. |author-link=Douglas N. Arnold |date=2018 |title=Finite Element Exterior Calculus|publisher=SIAM|isbn=978-1-611975-53-6}}</ref>
among others. 
<ref>Alan Demlow and Anil Hirani, [https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.0803 A posteriori error estimates for finite element exterior calculus: The de Rham complex], Found. Comput. Math. 14 (2014), 1337-1371.</ref> 
<ref>Christiansen, Snorre, and Ragnar Winther. "[https://www.ams.org/mcom/2008-77-262/S0025-5718-07-02081-9/S0025-5718-07-02081-9.pdf Smoothed projections in finite element exterior calculus]." Mathematics of Computation 77.262 (2008): 813-829.</ref> 
<ref>Christiansen, Snorre, and Francesca Rapetti. "[https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.4835 On high order finite element spaces of differential forms]." Mathematics of Computation 85.298 (2016): 517-548.</ref> 
<ref>Holst, Michael, Adam Mihalik, and Ryan Szypowski. "[http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/download?doi=10.1.1.766.8507&rep=rep1&type=pdf Convergence and optimality of adaptive methods in the finite element exterior calculus framework]." arXiv preprint arXiv:1306.1886 (2013).</ref> 
<ref>Holst, Michael, and Ari Stern. "[https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.4455 Geometric variational crimes: Hilbert complexes, finite element exterior calculus, and problems on hypersurfaces]." Foundations of Computational Mathematics 12.3 (2012): 263-293.</ref> 
<ref>Hiptmair, Ralf. "[https://www.ams.org/mcom/1999-68-228/S0025-5718-99-01166-7/S0025-5718-99-01166-7.pdf Canonical construction of finite elements]." Mathematics of Computation of the American Mathematical Society 68.228 (1999): 1325-1346.</ref>
<ref>Hiptmair, Ralf. "[https://web.archive.org/web/20190607170945/https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/cb77/bb244f3528c938c98ae3b5ebdc6cd33547f2.pdf Finite elements in computational electromagnetism]." Acta Numerica 11 (2002): 237-339.</ref> 
<ref>Kirby, Robert C. "[https://cpb-us-east-1-juc1ugur1qwqqqo4.stackpathdns.com/sites.baylor.edu/dist/6/32/files/2015/01/ssec-1zn3ii2.pdf Low-complexity finite element algorithms for the de Rham complex on simplices] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190607170951/https://cpb-us-east-1-juc1ugur1qwqqqo4.stackpathdns.com/sites.baylor.edu/dist/6/32/files/2015/01/ssec-1zn3ii2.pdf |date=2019-06-07 }}." SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 36.2 (2014): A846-A868.</ref> 
<ref>Licht, Martin Werner. [http://www.math.ucsd.edu/~mlicht/thesis.pdf On the A Priori and A Posteriori Error Analysis in Finite Element Exterior Calculus]. Diss. Dissertation, Department of Mathematics, University of Oslo, Norway, 2017.</ref>
Finite element exterior calculus is sometimes called as an example of a compatible discretization technique, and bears similarities with [[discrete exterior calculus]], although they are distinct theories.

One starts with the recognition that the used [[Differential operator|differential operators]] are often part of complexes: successive application results in zero. Then, the phrasing of the differential operators of relevant differential equations and relevant boundary conditions as a [[Hodge Laplacian]]. The Hodge Laplacian terms are split using the [[Hodge decomposition]]. A related [[Variational principle|variational]] [[Saddle point|saddle-point]] formulation for [[Mixed finite element method|mixed]] quantities is then generated. [[Discretization]] to a mesh-related subcomplex is done requiring a collection of [[Projection (linear algebra)|projection]] operators which [[Commutative property|commute]] with the differential operators. One can then prove uniqueness and optimal convergence as function of mesh density.

FEEC is of immediate relevancy for [[diffusion]], [[Elasticity (physics)|elasticity]], [[electromagnetism]], [[Stokes flow]]. 

For the important [[De Rham cohomology|de Rham complex]], pertaining to the grad, curl and div operators, suitable family of elements have been generated not only for tetrahedrons, but also for other shaped elements such as bricks. Moreover, also conforming with them, prism and pyramid shaped elements have been generated. For the latter, uniquely, the shape functions are not polynomial. The quantities are 0-forms (scalars), 1-forms (gradients), 2-forms (fluxes), and 3-forms (densities).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cockburn|first1=Bernardo|last2=Fu|first2=Guosheng|date=2017-01-01|title=A Systematic Construction of Finite Element Commuting Exact Sequences|url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/16M1073352|journal=SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis|volume=55|issue=4|pages=1650–1688|doi=10.1137/16M1073352|issn=0036-1429|arxiv=1605.00132|s2cid=38216995 }}</ref> Diffusion, electromagnetism, and elasticity,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Arnold|first1=Douglas N.|last2=Falk|first2=Richard S.|last3=Winther|first3=Ragnar|date=2007-10-01|title=Mixed finite element methods for linear elasticity with weakly imposed symmetry|url=https://www.ams.org/journal-getitem?pii=S0025-5718-07-01998-9|journal=Mathematics of Computation|volume=76|issue=260|pages=1699–1724|arxiv=math/0701506|  doi=10.1090/S0025-5718-07-01998-9|bibcode=2007MaCom..76.1699A |doi-access=free}}</ref> Stokes flow,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Falk|first1=Richard S.|last2=Neilan|first2=Michael|date=2013-01-01|title=Stokes Complexes and the Construction of Stable Finite Elements with Pointwise Mass Conservation|url=http://epubs.siam.org/doi/10.1137/120888132|journal=SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis|language=en|volume=51|issue=2|pages=1308–1326|doi=10.1137/120888132|issn=0036-1429|citeseerx=10.1.1.294.9104}}</ref> [[general relativity]], and actually all known complexes,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Finite element exterior calculus - 4 {{!}} Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences|url=https://www.newton.ac.uk/seminar/20190712140015001|access-date=2021-03-16|website=www.newton.ac.uk|date=5 March 2021 }}</ref> can all be phrased in terms of the de Rham complex. For [[Navier–Stokes equations|Navier-Stokes]], there may be possibilities too.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Fang|first=Shizan|date=2020-03-01|title=Nash Embedding, Shape Operator and Navier-Stokes Equation on a Riemannian Manifold|journal=Acta Mathematicae Applicatae Sinica, English Series|language=en|volume=36|issue=2|pages=237–252|doi=10.1007/s10255-020-0928-1|issn=1618-3932|arxiv=1907.13519|s2cid=199000940 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Samavaki|first1=Maryam|last2=Tuomela|first2=Jukka|date=2020-02-01|title=Navier–Stokes equations on Riemannian manifolds|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0393044019302244|journal=Journal of Geometry and Physics|language=en|volume=148|article-number=103543|doi=10.1016/j.geomphys.2019.103543|issn=0393-0440|arxiv=1812.09015|bibcode=2020JGP...14803543S |s2cid=119133831 }}</ref>
